sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the area between the Campania and Puglia regions, by the northern shoulder of the Vulture volcano, and belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This Source is a near-vertical, ca. N-dipping, fault to the east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a sparse intermediate seismicity in this region, but for the destructive earthquake of that has affected the western sector on 14 August 1851 (Mw 6.3, Basilicata).
This source is thought to be a deep, blind E-W fault system, a part of the tectonic mechanism that seems to characterize the entire seismogenic domain east of the southern Apennines backbone, and possibly of the central ones too. The western sector of this Source is thought to have caused the 1851 earthquake.
A segment of this Source has been associated with the 1851 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this source was based on that of the mapped subsurface structures. The dip was based on seismological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents right-lateral strike slip, based on seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on subsurface data. The slip rate was inferred from geodynamic considerations for the tectonic environment that includes this Source.
